clue.text: Tennessee's reincarnation of Nileville

parts.note: the US city in Tennessee shares its name with the ancient Egyptian capital on the Nile, so it is that city born again

explanation.surface: A whimsical note that a Tennessee town is an ancient Nile city come back to life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nileville' is a jokey coinage for a city on the Nile; the Egyptian capital of the Old Kingdom gave its name to the Tennessee city on the Mississippi.
explanation.definitionFit: The city in Tennessee was named after the ancient capital of Egypt beside the Nile, a namesake reborn.

clue.text: Sprightly as Hermes in Rome ?

definitions.meaning: lively, quick-changing and volatile in mood
the Greek messenger god Hermes was called Mercury by the Romans, so this means like Mercury

explanation.surface: Someone is as lively as the winged messenger god, Roman version.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermes's Roman name is Mercury, and the adjective from that god also means lively and changeable.

clue.text: Lamentation's non-U, so soon in the day

indicators.note: non-U says the letter U is to be dropped from the word for lamentation

parts.note: lamentation is grief, mourning

explanation.surface: A remark that grieving is socially lowbrow, and so early in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-U' is a British class label (not upper-class), but here it simply means 'without U'.
explanation.definitionFit: The early hours of the day before noon are the first part of daytime.

clue.text: Greeting with little point at Mac's celebration

parts.note: hallo is a greeting, a variant of hello
wee means small or little, a Scots word
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A Scot greets people with a tiny point of order at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mac' stands for a Scot; the eve of All Saints is a big festival in Scotland, and WEE is Scots for little.
explanation.definitionFit: The festival on 31 October, the eve of All Saints, is widely celebrated in Scotland with guising.

clue.text: Herb is a man of wisdom

definitions.meaning: a culinary herb with grey-green leaves

explanation.surface: Someone called Herb is said to be a wise man.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a kitchen herb of the mint family and a person of profound wisdom.

clue.text: Girl embraces boy at the plant

indicators.note: embraces means the girl's name wraps around the boy's

parts.note: Vera is a girl's name
Ben is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl hugs a boy beside a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Vervain and its relatives form a genus of flowering garden plants.

clue.text: Curiously loved piece, that old bicycle

indicators.note: curiously signals the letters of the next two words are arranged in an odd new way

explanation.surface: An odd, much-loved item turns out to be an antique bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curiously' rearranges LOVED PIECE.
explanation.definitionFit: An early pedal-driven bicycle such as the boneshaker was a nineteenth-century two-wheeler.

clue.text: It's vertical in certain flights

parts.note: flights here are flights of stairs, and the upright board between two treads is meant, not aircraft

explanation.surface: Something stands upright during some aeroplane journeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flights' suggests air travel; it means staircases.
explanation.definitionFit: In carpentry the upright face of each step in a staircase stands vertically between the treads.

clue.text: Suppression, of high priest on biblical mount

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the priest's name sits above the mountain's

parts.note: Eli was the high priest at Shiloh who raised Samuel
Sion, or Zion, is the hill of Jerusalem in the Bible

explanation.surface: A tale of a high priest silenced on a holy mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics, the omission or suppression of a sound or syllable, as in 'can't'.

clue.text: Pale as Dame. Partlet

parts.note: Dame Partlet is the hen in Chaucer's Nun's Priest's Tale, wife of Chanticleer the cock

explanation.surface: Someone is as white as a fabled farmyard lady.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Partlet is the traditional name for a hen in English fable.
explanation.definitionFit: A face drained of colour, grey like the residue of a fire, is pallid.

clue.text: Cobbett's rides were in the country

definitions.text: Cobbett's rides were in the country

parts.words: Cobbett's rides were in the country
parts.note: William Cobbett's 1830 book describes his horseback tours of English farmland, and its title adjective is wanted

explanation.surface: A note that William Cobbett's travels on horseback took place outside town.
explanation.walkthrough: William Cobbett was an English radical writer whose famous book is an account of tours on horseback through the farming counties.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobbett's book title uses the adjective for countryside as opposed to town, describing his rides.

clue.text: Oliver the metal worker ?

definitions.meaning: Oliver is the first name of the Irish author of The Vicar of Wakefield
a craftsman who works a precious yellow metal

explanation.surface: A man named Oliver is apparently a craftsman in metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver of She Stoops to Conquer had a surname naming a craftsman in gold.

clue.text: Agreement not to sing in parts

definitions.meaning: all voices singing the same melody together rather than in harmony

explanation.surface: Choir members agree they will not sing harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both concord between people and the singing of one tune together without harmony.

clue.text: Sanctimonious circle held in contempt. It has a sting

indicators.note: held in means the two short pieces sit inside the word for contempt

parts.note: scorn means contempt
pi is slang for pious or sanctimonious
O is shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: A self-righteous clique is despised, and its gossip stings.
explanation.definitionFit: This arachnid has a venomous stinger at the tip of its curled tail.

clue.text: Paddy's fairy shoemaker

parts.note: Paddy stands for an Irishman, and the Irish folklore sprite who mends shoes is meant

explanation.surface: An Irishman's magical cobbler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' is an old nickname for an Irishman.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish folklore this little sprite is a cobbler with a hidden crock of gold.

clue.text: Fireplace in Wardle's Dell

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the name of the place, not counting its outer letters

parts.note: Mr Wardle's home in Dickens's Pickwick Papers is Dingley Dell

explanation.surface: A hearth in a country character's dell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wardle's Dell' must first be turned into its full Dickens name, Dingley Dell; the answer sits in DINGLEY, between its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is a hearth or fire on a domestic hearth, as in ingle-nook.

clue.text: Pater's one translation into Zamenhof's tongue

indicators.note: a translation turns words into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, with its S

explanation.surface: A father's work rendered into an artificial language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation' rearranges PATERS ONE. L. L. Zamenhof invented the international language in 1887.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludwik Zamenhof devised this constructed international language as a universal second tongue.

clue.text: He tells a tale of Paris besieged by robots .

indicators.note: besieged by means the robots surround the tale

parts.note: R.U.R. is Karel Capek's play that introduced the word robot
conte is French for a short story

explanation.surface: A storyteller recounts a Parisian yarn about a city surrounded by machines.
explanation.walkthrough: R.U.R. (Rossum's Universal Robots) is the 1920 Czech play by Capek that gave English the word robot.
explanation.definitionFit: A storyteller is someone skilled at relating anecdotes in an entertaining way.

clue.text: Watchful domestic carries the old boy

indicators.note: in a down clue the servant carries the other piece on top, so it comes first

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a domestic is a household servant

explanation.surface: A vigilant housemaid helps the elderly gentleman along.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'carries' puts OB above SERVANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone attentive and alert notices things; vigilant.

clue.text: City nominally yielded by Peter to red leader in 1924

definitions.text: City nominally yielded by Peter to red leader in 1924

parts.words: City nominally yielded by Peter to red leader in 1924
parts.note: the Russian city founded by Peter the Great lost his name and took the Bolshevik leader's in 1924

explanation.surface: A city's name handed from a tsar to a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: St Petersburg (Petrograd) was renamed after the Bolshevik leader in 1924, the year of his death.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltic city founded by Tsar Peter was renamed after the Bolshevik leader in 1924.

clue.text: She engineered the fall which followed pride

definitions.text: She engineered the fall which followed pride

parts.words: She engineered the fall which followed pride
parts.note: pride goes before a fall, and the Greek goddess of retribution brought down the arrogant

explanation.surface: A woman plotted someone's downfall after their arrogance.
explanation.walkthrough: Plays on the proverb 'pride goes before a fall'; the Greek goddess of divine retribution punished hubris.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek goddess of retribution punished arrogance and hubris with downfall.

clue.text: Body of policemen surrounding the river

indicators.note: surrounding means the policemen go around the river letter

parts.note: cops are policemen
R is the abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A squad of police officers encircles the river.
explanation.definitionFit: An organised group such as an army unit or diplomatic group is an organised group of people.

clue.text: Could be a target for boat races

indicators.note: could be says the letters could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A rowing event might itself be a target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' rearranges A TARGET.
explanation.definitionFit: A series of rowing or sailing competitions held as one event.

clue.text: Stack of fruit in Eire ?

parts.note: a lime is a green citrus fruit
a rick is a stack of hay

explanation.surface: A pile of fruit seen somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a county and city in the Irish Republic, so somewhere in Eire; the '?' admits it.
explanation.definitionFit: A county and city in the Irish Republic, on the River Shannon in the west.

clue.text: Pure heart — but in a hat that's ghastly

indicators.note: in means the middle letters go inside the hat

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat

indicators.note: heart means the middle letters of the word pure

explanation.surface: Someone innocent at heart wears a hideous hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' takes UR from PURE, which goes 'in' LID.
explanation.definitionFit: Shocking or sensational, garish in a horrifying way.

clue.text: Lift beams, say

indicators.note: say tells us the beams word gives the answer when spoken

parts.note: rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: Instructions to hoist some timber joists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beams' looks like timber; it is light.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to lift it upward.

clue.text: Whereon a German conceals a wild ass

indicators.note: conceals means the answer is tucked inside the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A German stood on something that hides a wild donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The onager is a wild donkey of central Asia.

clue.text: Maintain a stronghold

definitions.meaning: to maintain is to retain or look after
the central tower of a castle

explanation.surface: Someone is told to defend a fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to retain or look after and the fortified central tower of a castle.

clue.text: Send down a sound country rowing team

parts.note: rustic means of the country

indicators.note: sound says the crew word is spoken and the spelling heard is entered

parts.note: an eight is a racing boat crew of eight rowers

explanation.surface: A strong country crew is expelled from the university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send down' is British university slang for suspend a student; 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning sturdy.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford and Cambridge, to suspend a student temporarily from college is to rusticate them.

clue.text: You won't get this off your own bat !

definitions.text: You won't get this off your own bat !

parts.words: You won't get this off your own bat
parts.note: in cricket some runs, such as byes and wides, are credited without the batsman hitting the ball

explanation.surface: A warning that you won't achieve something by your own efforts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off your own bat' is an idiom for independently; in cricket, runs from byes, leg byes, wides and no-balls are not scored by hitting.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a bye or wide is a run not hit by the batsman, added to the score.

clue.text: Distinguish, and maybe rescind

indicators.note: maybe signals the next word's letters may be shuffled into another word

explanation.surface: Tell the difference, and perhaps cancel it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges RESCIND.
explanation.definitionFit: To perceive or detect something by sight or mind is to make it out.

clue.text: Fairy with a tendency to charm

parts.note: a peri is a fairy of Persian legend
apt to do something means having a tendency to

explanation.surface: A fairy who is inclined to enchant people.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet or talisman worn to ward off harm.
